title: An Unweighted 71-Vertex Graph Admits a 33-Step Cycle of Inclusion-Minimal Profitable Deviations in Three-Color Max-Cut
abstract: In the max $k$-cut game each vertex of a graph chooses one of $k$ colors and earns the number of its neighbors with a different color. arXiv:1810.09278 showed on a weighted graph that improving deviations performed by minimal coalitions can cycle, so that weighted games admit no strong potential function even when only minimal coalitions may deviate; its concluding section leaves open whether a strong potential function exists on unweighted graphs. We answer this negatively for three colors. On an explicit unweighted graph with 71 vertices, made of four core blocks of eight vertices and three anchor blocks of thirteen, we give a cycle of 33 strong improvements that returns to its starting coloring: the 32 core vertices first deviate jointly, each gaining exactly one, and then return to their original colors one at a time, each again gaining one. Every step is inclusion-minimal: from the coloring where the step starts, no proper subset of the changing vertices has any profitable joint deviation. The joint step lowers the cut by 32 and each of the 32 single moves raises it by one. The definitions, the cycle and its minimality are verified in Lean 4.
introduction:
In a finite game a potential function is a real function on strategy profiles that strictly increases whenever a player improves its payoff by a unilateral change. A strong potential function strictly increases also under every strong improvement, that is, every joint change of strategy by a coalition in which all members strictly gain. Such a function forbids cycles of strong improvements and, when it exists, proves that strong equilibria exist, because the improvement dynamics must stop. It is one of the main tools for proving the existence of strong equilibria.

The max $k$-cut game is played on a finite undirected graph $G = (V, E)$. Each vertex is a player choosing one of $k$ colors, and its payoff is the total weight of its incident edges whose other endpoint has a different color; on an unweighted graph this is the number of differently colored neighbors. The cut value is an exact potential for unilateral moves, so Nash equilibria exist. Whether strong equilibria always exist is open.

arXiv:1810.09278 studies strong equilibria of this game. A strong improvement there is minimal if no proper subset of the deviating coalition can perform an improvement by itself. Its Proposition 2 exhibits a weighted graph with a cycle of strong improvements performed by minimal coalitions only (the joint deviation of four players followed by four single-player improvements), so that on weighted graphs no strong potential function exists even when only minimal coalitions are allowed to deviate. For unweighted graphs the paper proves positive results: from a Nash equilibrium, minimal strong improvements by coalitions of at most five players increase the cut value, and every optimal coloring is a 5-strong equilibrium. It also shows that the cut value itself is not a strong potential function on unweighted graphs. Its concluding section states that it is still unknown whether a strong potential function exists on unweighted graphs.

This post answers that question negatively for three colors, in the strong form of the weighted result. We give an explicit unweighted graph `maxcut_cycle71_graph` on 71 vertices and a sequence of 33 three-colorings that returns to its start, in which every step is a strong improvement by the set of vertices that change color, and every step is inclusion-minimal: from the coloring where the step starts, no proper subset of the changing vertices has any profitable joint deviation at all. A function that strictly increased along every minimal strong improvement would increase strictly around this cycle, which is impossible. So unweighted three-color max-cut games admit no strong potential function, even when only minimal coalitions may deviate.

The cycle has a simple shape. One step is a joint deviation of 32 core vertices that lowers the cut by 32 while each core vertex gains exactly one; the other 32 steps are single vertices returning to their old colors, each raising the cut by one. The whole construction is formalized and machine-checked in Lean 4 as `maxcut_unweighted_minimal_deviation_cycle_exists`.
result:
The main theorem establishes the existence of an infinite periodic sequence of strong deviations in the three-color Max-Cut game on the unweighted 71-vertex graph `maxcut_cycle71_graph`, returning to its initial profile after 33 steps, where every step is inclusion-minimal.

Theorem (`maxcut_unweighted_minimal_deviation_cycle_exists`).
There exists a decidable adjacency relation $d$ on `maxcut_cycle71_graph` and a sequence of three-colorings $f : \mathbb{N} \to (\text{Fin } 71 \to \text{Fin } 3)$ such that:
1. The sequence returns to its start after 33 transitions: $f(33) = f(0)$;
2. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the profile transition from $f(n)$ to $f(n+1)$ is a strong deviation (`is_maxcut_strong_deviation`) by the set of changing vertices, $S_n = \{ v \in \text{Fin } 71 : f(n+1)(v) \neq f(n)(v) \}$;
3. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the deviation $S_n$ is inclusion-minimal: for every proper subset $S \subsetneq S_n$, there exists no three-coloring $\tau : \text{Fin } 71 \to \text{Fin } 3$ such that $(S, \tau)$ is a strong deviation from $f(n)$ on `maxcut_cycle71_graph`.

What this result establishes: a strong potential function would strictly increase along every step of a sequence of strong improvements, so it cannot exist when such a sequence returns to its start. The theorem gives such a sequence on an unweighted graph with three colors, and every step of it is inclusion-minimal. Hence no strong potential function exists for the unweighted three-color max-cut game, even if it is only required to increase along strong improvements by minimal coalitions. This is the unweighted counterpart of Proposition 2 of arXiv:1810.09278 and answers the question its concluding section leaves open, for $k = 3$.
proof:
We outline the proof of `maxcut_unweighted_minimal_deviation_cycle_exists`. The sequence is $f(n) = \sigma_{n \bmod 33}$, where $\sigma_i$ is `maxcut_cycle71_return_stages` at $i$. Everything then reduces to one statement about the 33 consecutive pairs of stages.

Lemma 1 (`maxcut_cycle71_minimal_cycle_steps`). For every $i \in \text{Fin } 33$, with $i + 1$ taken in $\text{Fin } 33$, let
$$ D_i = \{ v \in \text{Fin } 71 : \sigma_{i+1}(v) \neq \sigma_i(v) \}. $$
Then $(D_i, \sigma_{i+1})$ is a strong deviation from $\sigma_i$, and for every proper subset $S \subsetneq D_i$ there is no coloring $\tau$ such that $(S, \tau)$ is a strong deviation from $\sigma_i$.

The 33 steps fall into two kinds: the joint deviation from stage 0 to stage 1, and the 32 single-vertex returns.

The single-vertex returns. For each of the 32 steps from stage $i$ to stage $i+1$ with $i \in \{1, \dots, 32\}$, a helper lemma checks by kernel evaluation that the set $D_i$ of changing vertices is the single core vertex $v_i$ of rank $i - 1$, and that $v_i$ strictly gains by returning from its $\sigma^{(1)}$ color to its $\sigma^{(0)}$ color, the rest of the coloring being fixed. In fact each such vertex gains exactly one, and each return raises the cut by one. Minimality is immediate here: the only proper subset of a singleton is empty, and a strong deviation requires a nonempty coalition.

The joint deviation. From stage 0 to stage 1 exactly the 32 core vertices change color, since the anchors have the same color in $\sigma^{(0)}$ and $\sigma^{(1)}$. That $(B_0 \cup B_1 \cup B_2 \cup B_3, \sigma^{(1)})$ is a strong deviation from $\sigma^{(0)}$ is again checked by kernel evaluation: every core vertex gains exactly one. For orientation, the degrees are 36 in $B_0$ (6 neighbors in $B_1$, 2 in $B_2$, 8 in $B_3$ and 20 anchors), 32 in $B_1$, 22 in $B_2$ and 34 in $B_3$; the cut drops from 688 edges to 656 at this step and climbs back by one per return.

Minimality of the joint deviation is the substantive part. Suppose a proper subset $S$ of the core and a coloring $\tau$ form a strong deviation from $\sigma^{(0)}$, and let $M \subseteq S$ be the members whose color actually changes. $M$ is nonempty: if no member changed color, $\tau$ would equal $\sigma^{(0)}$ and nobody would gain.

The argument rests on one finite count, checked by kernel evaluation: for each core vertex $v$ and each color $c \neq \sigma^{(0)}(v)$, the number of neighbors of $v$ that are core vertices or have a $\sigma^{(0)}$ color different from $c$ is at most $u_v(\sigma^{(0)})$, plus one if $c = \sigma^{(1)}(v)$. Since every vertex outside $S$ keeps its $\sigma^{(0)}$ color and $S$ lies in the core, this count bounds $u_v(\tau)$ for a member $v$ moving to $c$, whatever the other core vertices do. Two consequences follow for every $v \in M$:
- $v$ must move to its $\sigma^{(1)}$ color; any other new color gives $u_v(\tau) \le u_v(\sigma^{(0)})$.
- If $v$ has a core neighbor $w$ whose $\sigma^{(0)}$ color is $\sigma^{(1)}(v)$, then $w \in M$. Otherwise $w$ keeps that color, the edge $vw$ is monochromatic under $\tau$, and the bound drops by one to $u_v(\tau) \le u_v(\sigma^{(0)})$, so $v$ does not gain.

So $M$ is a nonempty set of core vertices closed under the forcing relation: $v$ forces each core neighbor whose initial color is $v$'s new color. Between blocks this relation goes $B_0 \to B_2$ (new color 2), $B_2 \to B_1$ (new color 1), $B_1 \to B_0$ and $B_1 \to B_3$ (new color 0), and $B_3 \to B_1$ (new color 1). A further lemma shows, by an explicit closed walk of 40 forcing steps through all 32 core vertices, that every nonempty closed set contains the whole core. Hence $M$, and with it $S$, contains all 32 core vertices, contradicting $S \subsetneq D_0$.

Proof of the main theorem. The decidability witness for adjacency is obtained by unfolding the definitions of `maxcut_cycle71_graph` and `maxcut_cycle71_field`. The sequence is $f(n) = \sigma_{\langle n \bmod 33 \rangle}$. Then $f(33) = f(0)$ holds by reflexivity, since $33 \bmod 33 = 0$. For any $n$, the stage index of $n + 1$ equals $i + 1$ in $\text{Fin } 33$ where $i$ is the index of $n$, by a short modular computation. So the step from $f(n)$ to $f(n+1)$ is the step from $\sigma_i$ to $\sigma_{i+1}$, and Lemma 1 at index $i$ gives both the strong deviation of the changing set and the absence of profitable deviations for its proper subsets.
discussion:
Theorem `maxcut_unweighted_minimal_deviation_cycle_exists` answers, for three colors, the question left open in the concluding section of arXiv:1810.09278: unweighted max-cut games admit no strong potential function, and this remains so when only minimal coalitions may deviate, as the paper had shown for weighted graphs. The weighted cycle there is a coalition of 4 followed by 4 single moves; here it is a coalition of 32 followed by 32 single moves. The anchor blocks of 13 vertices play the role of the heavy edges of the weighted example: they fix which colors each core vertex can profitably take.

Scope and Boundaries of the Result:

1. Colors: The counterexample operates in three-color Max-$k$-Cut ($k = 3$). The material does not address whether inclusion-minimal cycles can exist for two colors ($k = 2$). For $k = 2$ each player has a single alternative color, and the construction, which uses all three colors on the anchors, does not adapt directly.

2. Graph Order: The construction uses 71 vertices: 32 core vertices partitioned into four cyclic blocks of 8, and 39 anchor vertices partitioned into three blocks of 13. The result does not determine whether 71 vertices is the minimal graph size required to support an inclusion-minimal cycle, or whether a smaller unweighted graph could produce a similar cycle.

3. Graph Topologies: The construction of `maxcut_cycle71_graph` makes essential use of dense bipartite interconnections between core blocks and asymmetric connections to anchor blocks. The material does not cover structured graph families, such as planar graphs, graphs of bounded treewidth, or regular graphs.

What the construction shows. The cut value increases under every unilateral improvement, so any cycle of strong improvements needs coalitional steps that lower the cut. Here a single minimal coalition lowers it by 32, and 32 single moves, each a strict improvement, raise it back. The starting coloring $\sigma^{(0)}$ is not a Nash equilibrium (some anchor vertices can improve alone), so the cycle does not bear on the paper's cut-value argument for minimal coalitions of at most five players deviating from a Nash equilibrium; what it rules out is any strong potential function, which would have to increase along every strong improvement from every coloring. The question of whether every unweighted max $k$-cut game has a strong equilibrium, which the same paper leaves open with the conjecture that optimal colorings are strong equilibria, is not settled by this cycle: the cycle only rules out proofs of existence by a strong potential function.

Next Questions:

1. Does there exist an unweighted graph supporting a cycle of inclusion-minimal strong deviations for $k = 2$ colors?

2. What is the minimum number of vertices $n$ for which an unweighted graph admits an inclusion-minimal strong deviation cycle in three-color Max-Cut?

3. Can structural graph restrictions, such as planarity or bounded degree, guarantee the convergence of inclusion-minimal coalitional dynamics?
preliminaries:
Let $V$ be a finite vertex set and $G$ a simple graph on $V$. In a three-color Max-Cut game, each vertex chooses a color from $\{0, 1, 2\}$, formalized as $\text{Fin } 3$. The utility of vertex $v$ under coloring $\sigma : V \to \text{Fin } 3$ is the number of neighbors of $v$ assigned a color distinct from $\sigma(v)$:
$$ u_v(\sigma) = |\{ w \in V : G\text{.Adj}(v, w) \land \sigma(w) \neq \sigma(v) \}|. $$
Maximizing utility is equivalent to minimizing the number of neighbors sharing the same color.

Definition 1 (`is_maxcut_strong_deviation`). Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite type $V$ with decidable adjacency, and let $k \ge 1$. Given a profile $\sigma : V \to \text{Fin } k$, a coalition $S \subseteq V$, and a profile $\tau : V \to \text{Fin } k$, the predicate `is_maxcut_strong_deviation` holds if:
1. $S$ is nonempty;
2. $\tau(v) = \sigma(v)$ for all $v \notin S$;
3. $u_v(\sigma) < u_v(\tau)$ for all $v \in S$.

Remark on Definition 1. In arXiv:1810.09278 the members of a deviating coalition change their strategies. The Lean definition does not require this. Along the cycle below, each step's coalition is exactly the set of vertices whose color changes, so every member does change color. For minimality the Lean definition only makes the statement stronger: it rules out profitable deviations of proper subcoalitions in which members may also keep their colors.

Definition 2 (`maxcut_cycle71_field`). The anchor degree function `maxcut_cycle71_field` assigns the number of edges from core vertex $u$ to anchor block $j \in \{0, 1, 2\}$:
- For $u < 8$: 0 for $j=0$, 13 for $j=1$, and 7 for $j=2$.
- For $8 \le u < 16$: 1 for $j=0$, 2 for $j=1$, and 13 for $j=2$.
- For $16 \le u < 24$: 13 for $j=0$, 1 for $j=1$, and 2 for $j=2$.
- For $24 \le u < 32$: 0 for $j=0$, 7 for $j=1$, and 13 for $j=2$.
For $u \ge 32$, the field is 0.

Remark on Definition 2. Each anchor block has 13 vertices. A value of 13 connects $u$ to all vertices in that anchor block, while 0 creates no edges.

Definition 3 (`maxcut_cycle71_graph`). The graph `maxcut_cycle71_graph` is an unweighted simple graph on $V = \text{Fin } 71 = \{0, \dots, 70\}$. Vertices are partitioned into four core blocks of eight ($B_0 = \{0, \dots, 7\}$, $B_1 = \{8, \dots, 15\}$, $B_2 = \{16, \dots, 23\}$, $B_3 = \{24, \dots, 31\}$) and three anchor blocks of thirteen ($A_0 = \{32, \dots, 44\}$, $A_1 = \{45, \dots, 57\}$, $A_2 = \{58, \dots, 70\}$). An edge $\{u, v\}$ exists if and only if $u \neq v$ and $(R(u, v) \lor R(v, u))$, where $R(u, v)$ is the disjunction of six conditions:
1. $u \in B_0, v \in B_1$, and $(v - 8 + 8 - u) \pmod 8 \ge 2$;
2. $u \in B_0, v \in B_2$, and $(v - 16 + 8 - u) \pmod 8 < 2$;
3. $u \in B_0$ and $v \in B_3$;
4. $u \in B_1, v \in B_2$, and $(v - 16 + 8 - (u - 8)) \pmod 8 < 4$;
5. $u \in B_1, v \in B_3$, and $(v - 24 + 8 - (u - 8)) \pmod 8 \ge 2$;
6. $u < 32, v \ge 32$, and $(v - 32) \pmod{13} < \text{field}(u, (v - 32) / 13)$.

Remark on Definition 3. There are no edges within core blocks, between $B_2$ and $B_3$, or within/between anchor blocks. The conditions modulo 8 define regular cyclic connections among core blocks.

Definition 4 (`maxcut_cycle71_return_stages`). Let $\sigma^{(0)}$ and $\sigma^{(1)}$ be the two three-colorings that agree on the anchors, which are colored by block ($A_0$ color 0, $A_1$ color 1, $A_2$ color 2), and color the core blocks as follows: $\sigma^{(0)}$ gives $B_0, B_1, B_2, B_3$ the colors $0, 1, 2, 0$, and $\sigma^{(1)}$ gives them $2, 0, 1, 1$. The rank of a core vertex is its position in the order in which the core vertices return: first $B_3$, then $B_1$, then $B_2$, then $B_0$, each block in increasing order of vertices; ranks run over $\{0, \dots, 31\}$. For each $i \in \text{Fin } 33 = \{0, \dots, 32\}$, the profile $\sigma_i$ given by `maxcut_cycle71_return_stages` at $i$ is:
$$ \sigma_i(v) = \begin{cases} \sigma^{(0)}(v) & \text{if } i = 0 \lor (v < 32 \land \text{rank}(v) < i - 1), \\ \sigma^{(1)}(v) & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} $$

Remark on Definition 4. At stage 0 the coloring is $\sigma^{(0)}$. At stage 1 all 32 core vertices have their $\sigma^{(1)}$ colors. From stage $i$ to stage $i+1$, for $i = 1, \dots, 32$ (with stage 33 read as stage 0), the core vertex of rank $i - 1$ returns to its $\sigma^{(0)}$ color. The anchor vertices never change color.
research: Exhibits an unweighted three-color Max-k-Cut game with a cycle of inclusion-minimal profitable deviations, ruling out a strong potential even when deviations are restricted to minimal coalitions
tier_why: One explicit unweighted three-color instance settles the question left open in the concluding section of arXiv:1810.09278 (whether unweighted max-cut games admit a strong potential function), negatively and even for minimal coalitions, via a structured construction with a forcing argument; it is a side open question of a conference paper, not its central conjecture.

zh.title: 无权 71 顶点图在三色最大割中允许包含极小获益偏离的 33 步循环
zh.abstract: 在最大 $k$-割（Max-$k$-Cut）博弈中，图的每个顶点选择 $k$ 种颜色之一，其收益为具有不同颜色的邻居数量。arXiv:1810.09278 在带权图上表明，由极小联盟执行的改进偏离可能会成环，因此即使仅允许极小联盟进行偏离，带权博弈也不存在强势函数；其结论部分悬而未决的是无权图上是否存在强势函数。我们对三种颜色的情况给出了否定回答。在一个由 4 个 8 顶点核心块和 3 个 13 顶点锚块组成的 71 顶点显式无权图上，我们给出了一个返回其初始着色的 33 步强改进环：32 个核心顶点首先联合偏离，每个顶点收益恰好增加 1，然后逐个返回它们原本的颜色，每个顶点的收益再次增加 1。每一步都是包含极小的：从该步骤开始的着色出发，发生改变的顶点集的任何真子集都不存在任何有利的联合偏离。该联合步骤使割值降低 32，而 32 次单顶点移动中的每一次都使割值增加 1。相关定义、环及其极小性均已在 Lean 4 中得到验证。
zh.introduction:
在有限博弈中，势函数是策略配置上的实值函数，每当有玩家通过单方面改变而提高其收益时，该函数严格增加。强势函数在每次强改进下也严格增加，即联盟联合改变策略且其中所有成员的收益均严格增加。这样的函数禁止了强改进环的存在，并且在它存在时，证明了强均衡（SE）的存在，因为改进动态必然终止。它是证明强均衡存在性的主要工具之一。

最大 $k$-割博弈在有限无向图 $G = (V, E)$ 上进行。每个顶点作为一个玩家选择 $k$ 种颜色之一，其收益是与其关联且另一端点具有不同颜色的边的总权重；在无权图上，这就是具有不同颜色的邻居数量。割值是单方面移动的精确势，因此纳什均衡（NE）存在。强均衡是否始终存在仍然是一个公开问题。

arXiv:1810.09278 研究了该博弈的强均衡。在其中，如果发生偏离的联盟的任何真子集都无法自行实现改进，则称该强改进是极小的。其命题 2 展示了一个仅由极小联盟执行强改进形成环的带权图（四个玩家联合偏离，随后进行四次单玩家改进），从而表明在带权图上，即使只允许极小联盟进行偏离，也不存在强势函数。对于无权图，该论文证明了积极的结果：从一个纳什均衡出发，至多五个玩家的联盟进行的极小强改进会增加割值，并且每个最优着色都是 5-强均衡。它还表明，割值本身在无权图上并不是强势函数。其结论部分指出，无权图上是否存在强势函数仍然是未知的。

本文以带权图结果的强形式，对三种颜色的该问题给出了否定回答。我们给出了一个在 71 个顶点上的显式无权图 `maxcut_cycle71_graph` 以及一个返回起点的 33 个三着色序列，其中每一步都是改变颜色的顶点集所进行的强改进，并且每一步都是包含极小的：从该步骤开始的着色出发，发生改变的顶点集的任何真子集都根本没有任何有利的联合偏离。若一个函数沿每次极小强改进都严格增加，则它沿该环必须严格增加，这是不可能的。因此，无权三色最大割博弈不存在强势函数，即使仅允许极小联盟偏离也是如此。

该环具有简单的形式。其中一步是 32 个核心顶点的联合偏离，使割值降低 32，同时每个核心顶点的收益恰好增加 1；其余 32 步是单个顶点返回其原有颜色，每步使割值增加 1。整个构造已在 Lean 4 中形式化并经过机器检查，定理名称为 `maxcut_unweighted_minimal_deviation_cycle_exists`。
zh.preliminaries:
设 $V$ 为有限顶点集，$G$ 为 $V$ 上的简单图。在三色最大割（Max-Cut）博弈中，每个顶点从 $\{0, 1, 2\}$ 中选择一种颜色，形式化为 $\text{Fin } 3$。在着色 $\sigma : V \to \text{Fin } 3$ 下，顶点 $v$ 的效用是分配给与 $\sigma(v)$ 不同颜色的 $v$ 的邻居数量：
$$ u_v(\sigma) = |\{ w \in V : G\text{.Adj}(v, w) \land \sigma(w) \neq \sigma(v) \}|. $$
最大化效用等价于最小化共享相同颜色的邻居数量。

定义 1（`is_maxcut_strong_deviation`）。设 $G$ 是具有可判定邻接关系的有限类型 $V$ 上的简单图，并设 $k \ge 1$。给定策略配置 $\sigma : V \to \text{Fin } k$、联盟 $S \subseteq V$ 以及策略配置 $\tau : V \to \text{Fin } k$，当满足以下条件时，谓词 `is_maxcut_strong_deviation` 成立：
1. $S$ 非空；
2. 对所有 $v \notin S$，有 $\tau(v) = \sigma(v)$；
3. 对所有 $v \in S$，有 $u_v(\sigma) < u_v(\tau)$。

关于定义 1 的注记。在 arXiv:1810.09278 中，发生偏离的联盟的成员改变其策略。Lean 的定义并不要求这一点。在下文的环中，每一步的联盟恰好是颜色发生改变的顶点集，因此每个成员确实改变了颜色。对于极小性而言，Lean 的定义只会让结论更强：它排除了真子联盟可能获益的偏离，即使其中的成员保持其颜色不变也是如此。

定义 2（`maxcut_cycle71_field`）。锚度数函数 `maxcut_cycle71_field` 指定从核心顶点 $u$ 到锚块 $j \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ 的边数：
- 当 $u < 8$ 时：对于 $j=0$ 为 0，对于 $j=1$ 为 13，对于 $j=2$ 为 7。
- 当 $8 \le u < 16$ 时：对于 $j=0$ 为 1，对于 $j=1$ 为 2，对于 $j=2$ 为 13。
- 当 $16 \le u < 24$ 时：对于 $j=0$ 为 13，对于 $j=1$ 为 1，对于 $j=2$ 为 2。
- 当 $24 \le u < 32$ 时：对于 $j=0$ 为 0，对于 $j=1$ 为 7，对于 $j=2$ 为 13。
当 $u \ge 32$ 时，该场的值为 0。

关于定义 2 的注记。每个锚块有 13 个顶点。值为 13 表示将 $u$ 连接到该锚块中的所有顶点，而 0 则不产生任何边。

定义 3（`maxcut_cycle71_graph`）。图 `maxcut_cycle71_graph` 是 $V = \text{Fin } 71 = \{0, \dots, 70\}$ 上的无权简单图。顶点划分为四个 8 顶点的核心块（$B_0 = \{0, \dots, 7\}$、$B_1 = \{8, \dots, 15\}$、$B_2 = \{16, \dots, 23\}$、$B_3 = \{24, \dots, 31\}$）和三个 13 顶点的锚块（$A_0 = \{32, \dots, 44\}$、$A_1 = \{45, \dots, 57\}$、$A_2 = \{58, \dots, 70\}$）。边 $\{u, v\}$ 存在当且仅当 $u \neq v$ 且 $(R(u, v) \lor R(v, u))$，其中 $R(u, v)$ 是以下六个条件的析取：
1. $u \in B_0, v \in B_1$，且 $(v - 8 + 8 - u) \pmod 8 \ge 2$；
2. $u \in B_0, v \in B_2$，且 $(v - 16 + 8 - u) \pmod 8 < 2$；
3. $u \in B_0$ 且 $v \in B_3$；
4. $u \in B_1, v \in B_2$，且 $(v - 16 + 8 - (u - 8)) \pmod 8 < 4$；
5. $u \in B_1, v \in B_3$，且 $(v - 24 + 8 - (u - 8)) \pmod 8 \ge 2$；
6. $u < 32, v \ge 32$，且 $(v - 32) \pmod{13} < \text{field}(u, (v - 32) / 13)$。

关于定义 3 的注记。核心块内部、$B_2$ 与 $B_3$ 之间，以及锚块内部或相互之间不存在边。模 8 的条件定义了核心块之间的正则循环连接。

定义 4（`maxcut_cycle71_return_stages`）。设 $\sigma^{(0)}$ 和 $\sigma^{(1)}$ 为在锚块上一致的两种三着色，锚块按块着色（$A_0$ 着颜色 0，$A_1$ 着颜色 1，$A_2$ 着颜色 2），核心块着色如下：$\sigma^{(0)}$ 赋予 $B_0, B_1, B_2, B_3$ 颜色 $0, 1, 2, 0$，而 $\sigma^{(1)}$ 赋予它们 $2, 0, 1, 1$。核心顶点的秩为其在核心顶点返回顺序中的位置：依次为 $B_3$、$B_1$、$B_2$、$B_0$，每个块内部按顶点编号递增顺序排列；秩的取值范围为 $\{0, \dots, 31\}$。对于每个 $i \in \text{Fin } 33 = \{0, \dots, 32\}$，由 `maxcut_cycle71_return_stages` 在 $i$ 处给出的配置 $\sigma_i$ 为：
$$ \sigma_i(v) = \begin{cases} \sigma^{(0)}(v) & \text{if } i = 0 \lor (v < 32 \land \text{rank}(v) < i - 1), \\ \sigma^{(1)}(v) & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} $$

关于定义 4 的注记。在阶段 0，着色为 $\sigma^{(0)}$。在阶段 1，所有 32 个核心顶点均具有其 $\sigma^{(1)}$ 颜色。从阶段 $i$ 到阶段 $i+1$（对于 $i = 1, \dots, 32$，其中阶段 33 视作阶段 0），秩为 $i - 1$ 的核心顶点返回其 $\sigma^{(0)}$ 颜色。锚顶点从未改变颜色。
zh.result:
主定理确立了在无权 71 顶点图 `maxcut_cycle71_graph` 上的三色最大割博弈中，存在强偏离的无限周期序列，其在 33 步后返回到其初始配置，其中每一步都是包含极小的。

定理（`maxcut_unweighted_minimal_deviation_cycle_exists`）。
在 `maxcut_cycle71_graph` 上存在可判定邻接关系 $d$ 以及三着色序列 $f : \mathbb{N} \to (\text{Fin } 71 \to \text{Fin } 3)$，使得：
1. 该序列在 33 次转移后返回其起点：$f(33) = f(0)$；
2. 对每个 $n \in \mathbb{N}$，从 $f(n)$ 到 $f(n+1)$ 的配置转移是由发生改变的顶点集 $S_n = \{ v \in \text{Fin } 71 : f(n+1)(v) \neq f(n)(v) \}$ 执行的强偏离（`is_maxcut_strong_deviation`）；
3. 对每个 $n \in \mathbb{N}$，偏离 $S_n$ 是包含极小的：对于每个真子集 $S \subsetneq S_n$，不存在三着色 $\tau : \text{Fin } 71 \to \text{Fin } 3$ 使得 $(S, \tau)$ 是 `maxcut_cycle71_graph` 上从 $f(n)$ 出发的强偏离。

该结果所确立的内容：强势函数会沿着强改进序列的每一步严格增加，因此当这样的序列返回其起点时，强势函数不可能存在。该定理在具有三种颜色的无权图上给出了这样一个序列，且其每一步都是包含极小的。因此，对于无权三色最大割博弈，即使仅要求强势函数沿极小联盟的强改进增加，也不存在强势函数。这是 arXiv:1810.09278 命题 2 在无权图上的对应结论，并对 $k = 3$ 回答了其结论部分悬而未决的问题。
zh.proof:
我们概述 `maxcut_unweighted_minimal_deviation_cycle_exists` 的证明。该序列为 $f(n) = \sigma_{n \bmod 33}$，其中 $\sigma_i$ 是 `maxcut_cycle71_return_stages` 在 $i$ 处的值。于是所有内容都归结为关于 33 对连续阶段的一个命题。

引理 1（`maxcut_cycle71_minimal_cycle_steps`）。对于每个 $i \in \text{Fin } 33$（其中 $i + 1$ 取在 $\text{Fin } 33$ 中），令
$$ D_i = \{ v \in \text{Fin } 71 : \sigma_{i+1}(v) \neq \sigma_i(v) \}. $$
则 $(D_i, \sigma_{i+1})$ 是从 $\sigma_i$ 出发的强偏离，且对于每个真子集 $S \subsetneq D_i$，不存在着色 $\tau$ 使得 $(S, \tau)$ 是从 $\sigma_i$ 出发的强偏离。

这 33 步分为两类：从阶段 0 到阶段 1 的联合偏离，以及 32 次单顶点返回。

单顶点返回。对于从阶段 $i$ 到阶段 $i+1$（其中 $i \in \{1, \dots, 32\}$）的 32 步中的每一步，一个辅助引理通过内核求值验证了发生改变的顶点集 $D_i$ 是秩为 $i - 1$ 的单个核心顶点 $v_i$，并且在保持其余着色固定的情况下，$v_i$ 通过从其 $\sigma^{(1)}$ 颜色返回其 $\sigma^{(0)}$ 颜色而严格获益。事实上，每个这样的顶点的收益恰好增加 1，并且每次返回都使割值增加 1。这里的极小性是显而易见的：单元素集的唯一真子集是空集，而强偏离要求联盟非空。

联合偏离。从阶段 0 到阶段 1，恰好 32 个核心顶点改变颜色，因为锚顶点在 $\sigma^{(0)}$ 和 $\sigma^{(1)}$ 中具有相同的颜色。$(B_0 \cup B_1 \cup B_2 \cup B_3, \sigma^{(1)})$ 是从 $\sigma^{(0)}$ 出发的强偏离这一事实同样通过内核求值进行了验证：每个核心顶点的收益恰好增加 1。作为参考，度数在 $B_0$ 中为 36（$B_1$ 中有 6 个邻居，$B_2$ 中有 2 个，$B_3$ 中有 8 个，以及 20 个锚顶点），在 $B_1$ 中为 32，在 $B_2$ 中为 22，在 $B_3$ 中为 34；在这一步中，割值从 688 条边下降到 656 条边，并在随后的每次返回中逐一回升 1。

联合偏离的极小性是实质性的部分。假设核心的真子集 $S$ 与着色 $\tau$ 构成了从 $\sigma^{(0)}$ 出发的强偏离，并设 $M \subseteq S$ 为颜色实际发生改变的成员构成的集合。$M$ 是非空的：若没有成员改变颜色，则 $\tau$ 将等于 $\sigma^{(0)}$，没有人能够获益。

该论证依赖于通过内核求值验证的一项有限计数：对于每个核心顶点 $v$ 和每种颜色 $c \neq \sigma^{(0)}(v)$，$v$ 的为核心顶点或具有不同于 $c$ 的 $\sigma^{(0)}$ 颜色的邻居数量至多为 $u_v(\sigma^{(0)})$；若 $c = \sigma^{(1)}(v)$，则再加上 1。由于 $S$ 之外的每个顶点都保持其 $\sigma^{(0)}$ 颜色且 $S$ 位于核心内，无论其他核心顶点如何做，这一计数都界定了成员 $v$ 改变为颜色 $c$ 时的 $u_v(\tau)$。对每个 $v \in M$ 随之得出以下两个推论：
- $v$ 必须变为其 $\sigma^{(1)}$ 颜色；任何其他新颜色都会导致 $u_v(\tau) \le u_v(\sigma^{(0)})$。
- 若 $v$ 具有一个核心邻居 $w$，其 $\sigma^{(0)}$ 颜色为 $\sigma^{(1)}(v)$，则必有 $w \in M$。否则 $w$ 保持该颜色，边 $vw$ 在 $\tau$ 下为同色边，上界下降 1 变为 $u_v(\tau) \le u_v(\sigma^{(0)})$，从而 $v$ 无法获益。

因此，$M$ 是在强制关系（forcing relation）下封闭的核心顶点的非空集合：$v$ 强制其初始颜色等于 $v$ 的新颜色的每个核心邻居。在各个块之间，该关系的方向为 $B_0 \to B_2$（新颜色 2）、$B_2 \to B_1$（新颜色 1）、$B_1 \to B_0$ 和 $B_1 \to B_3$（新颜色 0），以及 $B_3 \to B_1$（新颜色 1）。另一个引理通过遍历所有 32 个核心顶点的 40 步强制步骤的显式闭途径表明，每个非空闭集都包含整个核心。因此 $M$（随之 $S$ 也）包含全部 32 个核心顶点，这与 $S \subsetneq D_0$ 矛盾。

主定理的证明。邻接关系的可判定性证明是通过展开 `maxcut_cycle71_graph` 和 `maxcut_cycle71_field` 的定义获得的。序列定义为 $f(n) = \sigma_{\langle n \bmod 33 \rangle}$。由于 $33 \bmod 33 = 0$，由自反性可知 $f(33) = f(0)$ 成立。对于任意 $n$，通过简短的模运算可知，$n + 1$ 的阶段指标等于 $\text{Fin } 33$ 中的 $i + 1$（其中 $i$ 是 $n$ 的指标）。因此从 $f(n)$ 到 $f(n+1)$ 的步骤即为从 $\sigma_i$ 到 $\sigma_{i+1}$ 的步骤，且引理 1 在指标 $i$ 处同时给出了发生改变的集合的强偏离以及其真子集不存在获益偏离的结论。
zh.discussion:
定理 `maxcut_unweighted_minimal_deviation_cycle_exists` 对三种颜色的情况回答了 arXiv:1810.09278 结论部分留下的公开问题：无权最大割博弈不存在强势函数，正如该论文对带权图所示的那样，即使仅允许极小联盟偏离，情况依然如此。文中的带权环是一个大小为 4 的联盟随后伴随 4 次单顶点移动；而这里的环是一个大小为 32 的联盟随后伴随 32 次单顶点移动。由 13 个顶点组成的锚块起到了带权示例中重边的作用：它们固定了每个核心顶点可以获益选择的颜色。

结果的范围与边界：

1. 颜色数：该反例在三色最大 $k$-割（Max-$k$-Cut，$k = 3$）中运作。本内容并未涉及二色（$k = 2$）情况下是否存在包含极小环。对于 $k = 2$，每个玩家只有一种备选颜色，而本构造在锚块上使用了全部三种颜色，无法直接推广。

2. 图的阶数：该构造使用了 71 个顶点：32 个核心顶点划分为四个大小为 8 的循环块，39 个锚顶点划分为三个大小为 13 的块。该结果并未确定 71 个顶点是否是支持包含极小环所需的最小图规模，或者更小的无权图是否也能产生类似的环。

3. 图的拓扑结构：`maxcut_cycle71_graph` 的构造实质性地利用了核心块之间的稠密二分相互连接以及与锚块的非对称连接。本内容未涉及结构化图族，例如平面图、有界树宽图或正则图。

该构造所表明的内容。割值在每次单方面改进下均会增加，因此任何强改进环都需要降低割值的联盟步骤。在此，单个极小联盟将割值降低 32，而 32 次单顶点移动（每次均为严格改进）又将其恢复。初始着色 $\sigma^{(0)}$ 不是纳什均衡（部分锚顶点可以单独改进），因此该环并不影响该论文中关于至多五个玩家的联盟从纳什均衡偏离的割值论证；它所排除的是任何强势函数，因为强势函数必须沿着从任何着色出发的每次强改进严格增加。同一论文留下的公开问题——每个无权最大 $k$-割博弈是否都具有强均衡（并猜想最优着色即为强均衡）——并未被该环解决：该环仅排除了通过强势函数证明存在性的途径。

后续问题：

1. 是否存在支持 $k = 2$ 种颜色的包含极小强偏离环的无权图？

2. 无权图在三色最大割中允许包含极小强偏离环的最小顶点数 $n$ 是多少？

3. 诸如平面性或有界度数等结构性图限制能否保证包含极小联盟动态的收敛性？
